N1.risk_note: Cheap GPU cells; removes the abstract overclaim that the screen lowers silent prices across models. Qwen may react to authority text alone, confounding the screen effect.

N2.risk_note: Tests causally whether the announced threshold is the focal price; Sonnet cells cost 4 to 7 USD each, so run Sonnet unannounced and threshold 5, Haiku both.

N3.risk_note: Run on Qwen only (GPU, under 1 USD); another paraphrase failure would weaken the fine result further but must be reported either way.

N4.risk_note: Haiku forms cartels in about 2 percent of leniency pair-periods; four more pools add only a handful of cartels, so cartel-level measures stay thin.

N5.risk_note: Red-teams the screen: a two-consecutive-period rule invites alternating high and low prices. Needs a pre-registered evasion metric; dual-use text must cover the found evasion.

why: N5 and N2 turn the screen from an observation into an adversarially tested control, the step a security reviewer wants; N1 and Qwen-only N3 are cheap GPU fixes for current overclaims. Claude spend about 22 USD, within budget.
missing_run: False-positive rate of the screen against LLM agents instructed to compete (no channel, Haiku and Qwen), not only scripted players, so the 1.1 percent claim holds for realistic legitimate agents.
